name: Völkisch movement
summary: The völkisch movement was a loose German ethno-nationalist current from the 1880s to 1933 that made race, descent and rootedness in the land the basis of the Volk, saw Jews as the chief enemy, and rejected democracy, parliamentarism, liberalism, socialism, pacifism and everything international. It sought a racially homogeneous, hierarchical national community and national rebirth, with imperial expansion into new living space, and never agreed on one manifesto (pagan and German-Christian wings, differing views on monarchy and industry).
scope: The movement of the Kaiserreich and Weimar Republic as the scholarship that defines the name describes it (Puschner's essay on the völkisch Weltanschauung, Maleszka, Tourlamain's study of its writers) and as set out in the texts those sources tie to it: Chamberlain's Foundations of the Nineteenth Century, Lagarde's Deutsche Schriften, Langbehn's Rembrandt als Erzieher and Heinrich Claß's Wenn ich der Kaiser wär' (1912). Puschner stresses that the movement never reached one ideological consensus or manifesto, so answers rest on what the scholarship says the movement as a whole held; points on which wings split (pagan against German-Christian religion, monarchy, industrialisation) are left unanswered or marked mixed. Nazism has its own entry and is not used; neither are the Pan-German League's or the DVFP's Wikipedia articles, which the earlier pass cited.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pacifism is named by Puschner as a danger.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inclusion was decided by race and descent (Puschner); Class's alien-law definition uses ancestry.

class-collaboration.rationale: The intended Volksgemeinschaft was a racial community set against socialism and capitalism alike, not a society of opposed classes (Puschner).

class-struggle-history.rationale: For völkisch thinkers race is the key to history (Puschner), and Chamberlain's history rests on racial struggle, not class.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: They envisioned one Reich covering all German-speaking Central Europe (Puschner).

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinism and racial hygiene informed the movement (Puschner), and Class quotes with approval that a people's development is struggle.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Materialism and capitalism are named dangers (Puschner), and Class has a chapter against materialism and Americanisation.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Germanic ideology grounds a paradigm of völkisch superiority and predestination (Puschner), and Chamberlain ranks races by creative worth.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy, parliamentarism and liberalism are named by Puschner among the things völkisch ideologues saw as dangerous developments; Class opposes equal universal suffrage.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Socialism and communism are named enemies (Puschner).

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Völkisch organisations demanded proof of Aryan descent, and the Judenordnung banned intermarriage (Puschner); Class defines Jews by descent, mixed ancestry included.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Puschner describes a virile gender hierarchy and a misogynist gender order as part of the völkisch social model.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The goal was racial homogeneity, with minorities seen as the cause of national ills (Puschner).

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Puschner speaks of a belief in their own superiority or even chosenness, religiously founded, though the neopagan wing held no god who chooses.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Judenordnung that Puschner calls a blueprint of the völkisch demands bans Jews from many professions and from owning land; Class wants Jewish influence excluded or cut back in all fields.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Puschner: everything international, from the League of Nations to the Church and masonry, was seen as a threat.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Puschner describes völkisch anti-humanism as stressing the essential, unbridgeable inequality of people and denying "lower" races dignity and human rights.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Puschner names a racially homogeneous Volksgemeinschaft, with membership by descent, as the goal völkisch ideologues imagined.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Puschner calls the race dogma dominantly biologistic; Chamberlain holds that inborn race decides creative capacity.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Puschner says eugenics and racial hygiene gave the movement decisive impulses, but he does not list a specific demand to bar people with heritable defects from having children.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Puschner: the blood-and-soil idea asserts a bond between race and land; Maleszka: the movement held that a person must be rooted in the native landscape.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Maleszka reports fear of industrial cities as a threat to the bond with nature, but Class's Germany is an industrial nation whose power he wants strengthened.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Puschner: early welcome of Zionism turned into vehement rejection of a Jewish state, which was said to become a power centre of the conspiracy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Materialism is rejected and race and spirit are the movement's explanatory keys (Puschner).

military-superiority.rationale: Class demands a strong army and navy and a Machtpolitik; the movement sought imperial dominance (Puschner).

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Jews, demonised as a counter-race, stood at the centre of völkisch agitation, and the Protocols of Zion escalated the movement's paranoia of a Jewish danger (Puschner).

nation-first.rationale: Radical nationalism and rejection of all internationalism and pacifism define the movement (Puschner).

national-rebirth.rationale: Völkisch writers spread decline-and-doom prophecies and offered renewal as the remedy (Puschner); Class's book calls for an inner turn.

natural-rulers.rationale: Puschner says they imagined an anti-egalitarian society led by a new racial nobility.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Capitalism, materialism and communism are all listed as dangerous developments (Puschner), with the Volksgemeinschaft as the alternative.

open-borders.rationale: Cosmopolitanism and everything international are named enemies and the goal is a racially homogeneous Volk (Puschner); Class demands closing borders to Jewish immigration.

organic-representation.rationale: Puschner says they imagined an occupationally organised (berufsständisch) society and attacked parliamentarism, parties and liberalism.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Puschner lists parliamentarism among the hated developments; Class (chapter on suffrage) wants the Kaiser to lead and to curb the equal Reichstag vote.

patriotic-education.rationale: Class says mothers should raise children to love the fatherland and treats civic education as a task.

population-transfer.rationale: The leading ideologues demanded disenfranchisement, segregation and expulsion (above all of eastern Jewish immigrants); Class demands that foreign Jews be expelled quickly and ruthlessly.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The national language and culture movement was a main source of the movement, and Pfister-Schwaighusen fought foreign words as a danger to German culture (Puschner).

purge-loanwords.rationale: The adjective völkisch was coined to replace "national", and its first promoter was a campaigner against foreign words (Puschner).

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: The Judenordnung forbids entry of foreign Jews and Class demands closing the borders to Jewish immigration; the Jews were defined as a race.

race-social-construct.rationale: Race is the basis of the worldview, taken as a real, hereditary reality (Puschner).

racial-franchise.rationale: Völkisch antisemitic programmes demanded undoing Jewish emancipation and alien-law status; the 1919 Judenordnung, which Puschner says formulated völkisch ideas, removed active and passive suffrage. Class's chapter "Die Juden unter Fremdenrecht" demands the same status.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Race is the glue of the movement and the key to everything (Puschner), with each racial group in struggle.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial self-confidence and a conviction of superiority are central (Puschner).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The leading ideologues demanded disenfranchisement, segregation and expulsion, and the Judenordnung excluded Jews from schools, universities and public baths (Puschner).

reason-over-faith.rationale: Puschner calls the worldview irrational and lists intellectualism among its enemies, with esoteric elements.

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: The movement demanded an arteigen religion (Puschner); Lagarde calls for national religions in the plural against one world religion, and Chamberlain names a faith compatible with Teutonic individuality as the Teuton's need.

religious-nation.rationale: Class defines "Jew" by descent and treats converts as Jews, so the national community is defined by race rather than by religion.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Puschner: the leading völkisch ideologues demanded exclusion, segregation and expulsion, above all of Jews who had immigrated from eastern Europe, and exclusion of Slavic groups such as the Poles living in the Reich; the 1919 Judenordnung they drew on required foreign Jews to leave within a month.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: Puschner records a German-Christian wing and a minority of neopagan Germanic believers who wanted to revive pre-Christian belief.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Maleszka reports the movement's view that city dwellers and urban trades lose the bond with nature and fear of industrial cities, with Puschner noting its agrarian society ideal.

sacred-nation.rationale: Puschner says they held their superiority and chosenness on (secular-)religious grounds and fused nation, race and religion.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Puschner: anti-humanism denies the value of humanisation and the equality of people.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Puschner describes a virile gender hierarchy, which does not leave marital authority equally shared.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Pacifism is a listed enemy, and Class condemns peace longing.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Materialism is condemned and idealism praised (Puschner; Class chapters "against materialism" and "German idealism").

strong-leader.rationale: Class says the times need a strong leader who forces recovery, and his book looks to the Kaiser as leader.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The superiority paradigm legitimised imperial claims and the conquest of new living space, especially in Eastern Europe (Puschner); Class's power-politics chapter plans expansion to the south-east.

traditional-family.rationale: Class calls on women to keep the home pure and raise children as patriots; Puschner notes the movement's male-dominated gender order.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Germanic ideology posits a biological line of descent from the ancient (Indo-)Germans to the Germans (Puschner).

war-builds-character.rationale: Class laments an unmanly longing for peace and cites approvingly the line that a people's development is struggle.

women-suffrage.rationale: Class says there must be no political women's question and rejects women's political claims, though he allows social work by women.

workers-councils.rationale: Socialism and communism, and democracy and parliamentarism, are rejected (Puschner).

missingStatements.text: The nation's identity should be rooted in a revived pre-Christian ancestral religion rather than in the Christian churches.
missingStatements.rationale: The common core of the movement was national rebirth on reconstructed Germanic traditions, with adherents wanting either a Germanized Christianity or a revived Germanic paganism (the pagan wing answers +2, the Christian wing -1).
missingStatements.declined: A single strand of one movement; no other ideology would take a position on a revived pre-Christian national religion, and national-rebirth covers the theme.

missingStatements.text: Members of a particular ethnic minority should have fewer civil and political rights than the majority.
missingStatements.rationale: Claß writes that the rights of the resident Jewish population must be generally restricted, even when the good suffer with the bad, because race is the source of the danger.

missingStatements.text: A nation's land and its people are bound together, and its peasantry is the source of its strength.
missingStatements.rationale: The article names blood and soil and agrarianism among the movement's concepts, and Langbehn wanted Germany to abandon industrialization and urbanization for an agrarian society.

notes: Later pass on rules 7. The first pass rested on Wikipedia articles and one Claß excerpt, so its answers were inferences; this pass keeps only answers a defining source states (Puschner's essay, Maleszka, Chamberlain, Claß, Lagarde, Tourlamain) and nulls the rest with the old version kept in reviewHistory. Themes searched in the local library: economy, ecology, technology, government institutions, religion, gender, war and world order; the bank's economy, ecology, technology and most government statements have no stated völkisch position. Claß's book is Fraktur OCR, so passages were relied on only where clear. The movement never agreed on one programme (Puschner), so splits are left null.
